subject: Remove low or higher value of correlation

messages.author: c89471eda5dca12c
messages.subject: Remove low or higher value of correlation
parts:
Hello 

I generated a correlation matrix using graph::cor_auto with the command 
"data.corr <- qgraph::cor_auto(Mydata, detectOrdinal = TRUE, ordinalLevelMax = 7, npn.SKEPTIC = FALSE, forcePD = TRUE, missing = "pairwise", verbose = TRUE)"

I observed I have a lot of low correlations:

    Var1 Var2         Corr
354 IG02 P008  0.001819839
374 P008 IG02  0.001819839
52  R02C G008  0.002024480
192 G008 R02C  0.002024480
228 IG02 R2B1 -0.003377963
368 R2B1 IG02 -0.003377963
289 P007 RDPL  0.006110177
329 RDPL P007  0.006110177

How I can remove these correlations before lavaan::sem(inputModel, sample.cov = data.corr, sample.nobs = nrow(data)) or correlations very high?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Remove low or higher value of correlation
parts:
Why are you doing this?  Not only is it a problem to fit a model to a correlation matrix instead of a covariance matrix:

http://www.statpower.net/Content/319SEM/Reading/Cudeck89.pdf

But if you estimate polychoric correlations first, then fit a model to those correlations, your results will be biased because you will not have taken into account the uncertainty about the estimated correlations.  It would be even more dishonest to change correlations to exactly zero just because they are close to zero, because then you don't even have estimates anymore, nor the estimated uncertainty necessary to account for in Step 2.  Instead, just fit your model to your raw data, specifying which variables should be treated as ordinal:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

lavaan will estimate the polychoric correlations automatically and take their uncertainty into account.  

Note that robust ML estimation may provide unbiased estimates with 5-7 categories, depending how asymmetric the thresholds are.

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Remove low or higher value of correlation
parts:
Elias,
If you have sufficient confidence in your model that ill fit leads you to first question the data, then it may be that there is nothing to be gained from fitting the model to the data.  The usual situation is the opposite: We are more confident in the data than the model and use the data to test the model.  Resolving ill fit is not a simple mechanical process like replacing the batteries in a flash light.  It is instead a complex highly-context-specific task of scientific inference that takes experience, skill, and practice.  If you have not done so already, I would highly recommend consulting a detailed introduction to this process such as can be found in Rex Kline's text "Principles and Practice of Structural Equation Modeling".  Be sure to obtain the 4th edition.  A general strategy might be to build up the model piece by piece in an attempt to localize the sources of ill fit.  However, if you think that you might be reading the data incorrectly, first compare the sample statistics from the lavaan fit object to the corresponding statistics obtained outside of lavaan by using lavInspect() to extract the statistics from the fit object.

Keith
